content.title: About
content.content: Gummy candy is a sweet treat made from gelatin, sugar, fruit or berry flavorings, and colorants. It has a soft, chewy texture and a bright, fruity flavor profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first gummy-like sweets appeared in ancient Rome, using honey and fish-derived gelatin.
Modern gummies often use plant‑based gelling agents such as pectin instead of animal gelatin.
Bright colors are frequently obtained from natural extracts, but mass production relies on synthetic food dyes.
In Japan, “gummy‑med” coated with powdered sugar change flavor as you chew.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The sugar provides a rapid increase in blood glucose, delivering an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Fruit flavorings may contribute a small amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sweet taste stimulates serotonin production, helping to improve mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can lead to weight gain, tooth decay, and blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to gelatin, especially when it is animal‑derived.

items.title: Synthetic colorants
items.content: Certain food dyes have been linked to hyperactivity in children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gummy candy is convenient as a standalone snack, can be added to dessert mixes, used in baking, or as decorative toppings for cakes and cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package, protecting from moisture and direct sunlight. Properly stored, they retain shape and flavor for up to 12 months.
